subject: Potential restrictions in data size for spde models ?

messages.author: c4394a4e9fdc74a3
messages.subject: Potential restrictions in data size for spde models ?
parts:
Dear all,

I currently work on my Master thesis and try to fit a spde space-time model similar to the model described in Cameletti et al (2012), but my R code always runs into errors when I use larger data sets, even though it should not be a memory issue. So far the model is based on daily data (456 days) from 10 monitoring stations and I use a very rough mesh with 25 knots only. However, whenever I extend the model (more days, more stations or a finer mesh) inla.exe crashes even before the optimisation starts.
I do not think that it is an R code problem as I do not change any lines in the spde construction but only extend the model by adding several days. Also, holding the length of the time period constant but shifting it does not result in any errors.

Is there something like a maximum data size for INLA ? I am happy to send code and data on request and I hope to find help in this group. Thank you in advance!

Best,
Stephan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Potential restrictions in data size for spde models ?
parts:
The main limit is the size of your RAM.
If you're running on a multicore system, then reducing the number of allowed threads (num.threads in the inla() call) will reduce the required memory.

Finn

messages.author: c4394a4e9fdc74a3
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Potential restrictions in data size for spde models ?
parts:
Hi Finn,

thank you for your quick response! I already ran with verbose= TRUE, which was not very informative to me as the ouput always stops at a different line but always after the data is parsed and before the optimisation starts. I also set num.threads differently and tried out the code on different computers with much more RAM.
In the current set up (holding mesh resolution and number of stations constant) the problem always occurs when I add more days. To be presice, I found that the program always crashes when the "covariate lists" produced by the inla.stack.data() command have more than 9600 entries. If I reduce the data by one day only, so that the lists have less than 9600 entries, the program runs in ~40 sec.

Stephan
